title: Scottish National Gallery: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works ranging from an effortless-looking skate to the effort of mourning.
introduction:
The skater keeps his arms folded while one leg extends behind him. What appears easy is a carefully maintained balance. In Raphael’s Madonna, a turning child is held securely; in Hamilton’s mourning scene, a dead body must be supported by others. These are different uses of bodily weight, and they offer a thread through a selection that spans sacred subjects, portraits and landscapes.

The still lifes and river views extend the comparison. A black bottle steadies a loose arrangement of objects; poplars and their reflections repeat without becoming identical. Balance is a relation among unequal parts, not simply another name for symmetry or calm.
visitNote: The guide selects works associated with the National Galleries of Scotland’s collection. Check each object’s current building and display status when planning a visit: loans and installations can move works between sites or into storage. Pastels and other works on paper are especially likely to rotate.

books.title: Seven Discourses on Art
books.author: Joshua Reynolds
books.note: Reynolds’s Discourses record an eighteenth-century argument about the ambitions and methods of painting. Read them alongside Raeburn and Hamilton, while keeping their prescriptive account distinct from the very different later pictures here.

works.title: The Skating Minister
works.catalogueTitle: The Skating Minister (The Reverend Robert Walker Skating on Duddingston Loch)
works.credit: Sir Henry Raeburn. The Skating Minister (The Reverend Robert Walker Skating on Duddingston Loch). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The folded arms make the extended leg and narrow contact with the ice more conspicuous. The museum identifies the sitter cautiously as probably the Reverend Robert Walker and notes that the seemingly easy manoeuvre requires skill. The portrait obtains its character from that discrepancy: composure is visible, while the work of balance is largely concealed.

works.title: The Monarch of the Glen
works.credit: Edwin Landseer. The Monarch of the Glen. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The stag stands above the surrounding landscape with its antlers outlined against the sky. The low viewpoint gives the animal a commanding position usually associated with a formal human portrait. Its authority is produced by scale and placement; the mountain setting participates in that presentation rather than simply supplying a natural home.

works.title: Vision after the Sermon
works.catalogueTitle: The Vision after the Sermon (Jacob wrestling with the Angel)
works.credit: Paul Gauguin. The Vision after the Sermon (Jacob wrestling with the Angel). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The white-capped women and distant wrestlers share a red field, but do not occupy it on ordinary naturalistic terms. A diagonal tree divides them, and their scales differ abruptly. Gauguin lets the vision coexist with its witnesses while making the relationship visibly constructed. The colour refuses to behave as neutral ground.

works.title: An Old Woman Cooking Eggs
works.credit: Diego Velázquez. An Old Woman Cooking Eggs. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/diego-velazquez/an-old-woman-cooking-eggs-1618
works.description: Faces and utensils receive comparably exact attention in the close kitchen space. The boy’s offerings and the woman’s work connect glass, food and cooking vessel through practical handling. Velázquez does not leave these materials as incidental accessories. Their different surfaces give the ordinary task much of its substance.

works.title: Bridgewater Madonna
works.credit: Bridgewater Madonna. WikiArt; Raphael. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The child turns across Mary’s lap, introducing a movement her hands must contain. A dark setting makes the two bodies’ relation especially clear. The group remains stable because support answers the twist: the devotional image depends on a recognisable act of holding, not only on the identities of mother and child.

works.title: Fable: A Boy Lighting a Candle with an Ape and a Fool
works.catalogueTitle: Allegory, boy lighting candle in the company of an ape and a fool - Fábula
works.credit: El Greco. Allegory, boy lighting candle in the company of an ape and a fool - Fábula. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/el-greco/allegory-boy-lighting-candle-in-the-company-of-an-ape-and-a-fool-f%C3%A1bula
works.description: The flame gathers an ape, a boy and an older man into one small area of light. Their differences become visible through a common attraction. Before any allegorical interpretation is supplied, the picture establishes a physical relation between illumination and proximity: the heads emerge because they have approached the same source.

works.title: Autumn in Glencairn, Moniaive
works.credit: James Paterson. Autumn in Glencairn, Moniaive. Image credit: James Paterson; Source credit: https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/5679/autumn-glencairn-moniaive?page=1&search_set_offset=79. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The stream gives a pale route through browns and other closely related tones. Autumn does not require a single emblematic tree; changes accumulate across vegetation, fields and reflections. The water keeps the landscape open enough to follow, while low hills and cloud maintain its subdued scale.

works.title: Boy with a Horse
works.credit: Boy with horse. WikiArt; Georges Seurat. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Abbreviated strokes establish bodies, bank and opposite shore without resolving every surface. Their positions are sufficient to make the riverside occupied. The small work rewards attention to arrangement before finish: a horse, a boy and other figures can define intervals within an open place without becoming separate, fully described portraits.

works.title: Confirmation
works.credit: Confirmation. WikiArt; Nicolas Poussin. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The sacrament unfolds through a sequence of bodily positions: waiting, approaching and receiving. Bright clothing helps distinguish places within the darker architecture. Poussin makes ceremony intelligible as ordered action, allowing the group to share a space without requiring every participant to occupy the same moment of the rite.

works.title: Mars and Venus
works.credit: Mars and Venus. WikiArt; Paolo Veronese. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: Armour and soft clothing give the close encounter contrasting surfaces. Mars and Venus are connected by posture and touch, with Cupid adding another relation below. The mythological names identify the participants, but the material contrast does additional work: hardness and yielding fabric remain in immediate contact.

works.title: Mrs Ernest Hill
works.catalogueTitle: Mrs. Ernest Hill (Constance Malanie Wynne Roberts)
works.credit: John Singer Sargent. Mrs. Ernest Hill (Constance Malanie Wynne Roberts). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/john-singer-sargent/mrs-ernest-hill-constance-malanie-wynne-roberts
works.description: Dark dress and surrounding shadow occupy broad areas, making the pale trim and resting hand unusually important. Those limited accents describe both the sitter’s clothing and the adjustment of her pose. Sargent does not need equal illumination everywhere; the portrait’s presence depends on where distinctions become clear.

works.title: Oban
works.credit: James Guthrie. Oban. Image credit: James Guthrie; Source credit: https://www.nationalgalleries.org/art-and-artists/4999/oban?page=1&search_set_offset=90. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The curve of the waterfront organises a town built from broad, related greys. A pale promenade leads through the scene, while boats give the subdued water points of scale. Guthrie keeps the topography legible without individually detailing every building. The route along the shore holds the larger masses together.

works.title: The Black Bottle
works.credit: Samuel Peploe. The Black Bottle. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/samuel-peploe/the-black-bottle-1905
works.description: The bottle supplies one firm dark vertical among rounded objects and folded white cloth. It steadies the arrangement while making differences within the whites easier to notice. The small still life has no need of a narrative event: contrasts of weight, height and light provide enough relations to sustain looking.

works.title: The Feasts of Venice
works.credit: The Feasts of Venice. WikiArt; Jean-Antoine Watteau. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The dance does not absorb every figure’s attention in the same way. Companions, performers and onlookers occupy different positions around the garden and fountain. A pale dress supplies a strong accent without making the whole gathering uniform. Festivity appears as several kinds of participation, not one emotion assigned to an entire crowd.

works.title: Virgin and Child with Saints Jerome, Peter, Clare and Francis
works.catalogueTitle: Virgin and Child with Saints Jerome, Peter, Clare and Francis
works.credit: Lorenzo Lotto. Virgin and Child with Saints Jerome, Peter, Clare and Francis. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/lorenzo-lotto/virgin-and-child-with-saints-jerome-peter-clare-and-francis-1505
works.description: The reaching child and nearby saints form a close exchange of hands and faces. A narrow landscape remains above them, but little space separates the principal bodies. Saints from different histories share a devotional arrangement here; their proximity should be read as the image’s construction rather than evidence of a single historical meeting.

works.title: Snow Scene at Moret Station
works.credit: Alfred Sisley. Snow Scene Moret Station. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/alfred-sisley/snow-scene-moret-station-1888
works.description: Dark branches and narrow fences interrupt the snow’s broad light surface. Softer pastel marks keep buildings and winter air closely related, avoiding the effect of objects cut sharply out of a uniformly white ground. Sisley differentiates the place through limited contrasts, letting reduced visibility become part of its character.

works.title: Christ Blessing
works.catalogueTitle: Christ Blessing (The Saviour of the World)
works.credit: El Greco. Christ Blessing (The Saviour of the World). Image credit: El Greco; Source credit: 2. Scottish National Gallery 1. Google Arts & Culture. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The raised hand establishes a blessing as clearly as the face establishes a direct address. Red and blue drapery give the elongated figure a restrained setting, while the globe belongs to its sacred role. The picture’s relation to the spectator differs from an ordinary likeness: the gesture actively accompanies the gaze.

works.title: Poplars on the Epte
works.credit: Claude Monet. Poplars on the Epte. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The trunks repeat above the bank and continue below it in reflections that are less stable. Similar verticals receive different colours and surrounding marks, so repetition never becomes exact duplication. Monet uses the row to make variation legible; the water supplies a second, shifting account of the same structure.

works.title: The Marne at Chennevières
works.credit: Camille Pissarro. The Marne at Chennevières. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The river lies between a wooded bank and distant settlement, with boats and buildings offering small measures of human occupation. Broad divisions of water, land and sky keep those details from fragmenting the view. The landscape remains open, but its openness belongs to a place used and inhabited.

works.title: Achilles Lamenting the Death of Patroclus
works.catalogueTitle: Achilles Lamenting the Death of Patroclus
works.credit: Gavin Hamilton. Achilles Lamenting the Death of Patroclus. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The dead body provides a diagonal toward which the surrounding gestures are directed. Achilles bends close, while companions supply support the body can no longer give itself. Hamilton gives mourning the scale of a public history painting, but the principal relation remains physical: grief gathers around weight that others must carry.

closingSections.title: Choose comparisons before choosing a route
paragraphs: The skater, Raphael’s child and Hamilton’s dead warrior offer three distinct conditions of bodily support. They need not be seen as one chronological argument. Check individual venue and display information: Scotland’s national collection is presented across different buildings, and a work associated with this guide may currently be shown elsewhere in that network.
